class.name: FellowMotionCharacter3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: a character whose whole-body motion a neural network generates (MotionBricks SOMA on the GPU).
class.description: Set [member desired_velocity] every frame and the character walks, jogs, runs, turns and stops by itself — no animation clips. Its motion is generated in segments of 0.6-1.9 s by a [FellowMotionModel] ([member model_path]): each segment from the four poses the character last showed towards a target [member lead_time] ahead along the smoothed desired velocity, facing it and moving at it (the root only: the model fills in the body). The next segment is requested before the current one's transition point ([member transition_early_frames] before its end, or when the speed or the direction changes enough) and crossfaded in over [member crossfade_time] when it arrives. With a zero velocity it comes to rest in a relaxed stance and keeps generating small idle segments ([member idle_motion]). Every character naming one model file shares one model and its GPU device: their requests run as one batch ([member inference_mode]). The node moves itself: its origin follows the hips on the ground (at the height it started at), its +Z the facing. [member body_path] loads a skinned body (the SOMA mannequin [code]tools/fmb_usd.py[/code] writes) whose skeleton it poses; the model's 30 joints drive it, the hands keep a relaxed pose. The motion follows MotionBricks' runtime (context sampling from the recorded poses, endpoint correction, MovementControl's springs and regeneration rules). See [code]docs/decisions/0143-neural-motion.md[/code].

method.name: advance
method.description: Steps the character by [param delta] seconds (what the process callback does when [member auto_process] is on).

method.name: flush_requests
method.description: Runs every request waiting for the model (those of the characters in [constant INFERENCE_FLUSH] mode) as batches on the calling thread.

method.name: get_actual_velocity
method.description: The ground velocity the character showed in the last step.

method.name: get_error
method.description: Why the character does not move (no model, a model without a skeleton...), or empty.

method.name: get_joint_positions
method.description: The world positions of the skeleton's joints in the pose shown.

method.name: get_service_stats
method.description: The shared model's requests, batches, average batch size and time, the last batch's.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Generations, request latency, state, smoothed speed, the current segment's frames.

method.name: is_ready
method.description: Whether the model is loaded and the character placed.

members.member: Step in the process callback; off, call [method advance].
A glTF (.glb) with the SOMA skeleton and a skinned mesh, loaded at run time (once per file).

While the speed shown is far from the target's (by a quarter, at least 0.3 m/s: accelerating or braking), request a new segment every 0.33 s instead of at the transition point (the model approaches a target over its whole segment, up to 1.9 s).
How long a new segment takes to replace the one playing when it arrives later than requested.
Where and how fast to go (its ground part; up to [member max_speed]). Zero stops.
Standing still, keep generating small idle segments (off: the last pose holds).
How far ahead the target is placed, in seconds of the desired velocity.
The largest batch of the shared model (taken from the first character that loads it).
The longest segment the model may choose, in tokens of four frames (6-16).
The shortest segment the model may choose, in tokens of four frames (6-16).

How fast the target's speed follows [member desired_velocity]'s (a critically damped spring's halflife; the direction follows in 0.2 s). Starting to move, the target is at once at the desired speed: the model accelerates over the segment.
How many frames before a moving segment's end the next one takes over.

constants.constant: The model's worker thread runs the requests as they come; results on a later frame.
Requests wait for [method flush_requests] (all characters' as one batch); results the next step. Deterministic.
Each request runs at once on the calling thread (a batch of one; no latency).
